A function is continuous at every point where it has a derivative.

Theorem 1 says that if a function has a discontinuity at a point (for instance, a jump discontinuity), then it cannot be differentiable there. The greatest integer function y = :x; fails to be differentiable at every integer x = n (Example 4, Section 2.5).
Caution The converse of Theorem 1 is false. A function need not have a derivative at a point where it is continuous, as we saw with the absolute value function in Example 4.
